issues.legal_issue: An adoption by a widow relates back to the adoptive father's death, subject to the rule that an adopted child cannot divest an estate vested before the adoption and is bound by lawful prior alienations.
A widow's valid sale of property in which she acquired absolute ownership under a compromise decree binds her adopted son, who cannot challenge the sale for lack of his consent.
A valid gift requires acceptance by or on behalf of the donee, and a registered gift deed without evidence of acceptance is null and void.
A first appellate court may not overturn a trial court's sound finding on a definite issue without sustainable reasons grounded in its reappraisal of the evidence.
